# v_ase

> An ASE-native workspace for building, inspecting and rendering atomic structures, trajectories and scalar fields. An external agent and the researcher share the same live document.

## Agent setup

This guide describes v_ase 0.5.1. Match the Python runtime, desktop app, MCP adapter and Skill to the same release or development source ref.

- Setup guide: https://v-ase.readthedocs.io/en/latest/agent-setup.html
- Scientific Skill: https://github.com/lgyEthan/v_ase/tree/main/v_ase/skills/visualizing-atomic-structures-with-v-ase
- MCP connection guide: https://v-ase.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai-tools.html
- CLI and HTTP bridge: https://v-ase.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai-cli.html

Install the current source Skill for the coding clients the user selects:

```bash
npx skills@latest add lgyEthan/v_ase@v0.5.1 --skill visualizing-atomic-structures-with-v-ase -a claude-code codex cursor -g -y
```

The command installs instructions and their references. Install/configure the v_ase runtime and MCP connection separately. Use only the clients and project/global scope requested by the user; preserve unrelated MCP servers and existing environment configuration.

For the published 0.5.1 runtime, install `v_ase-gui[mcp]==0.5.1` and use the matching Skill tag. Older runtimes use their corresponding tag. For current GitHub source in a Python environment:

```bash
python -m pip install "v_ase-gui[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/lgyEthan/v_ase.git@main"
```

Reuse an existing GUI through its copied agent connection URL. If starting an owned GUI for the requested task, expose its human URL and keep it connected. Discover the live tools/schema, read the scientific Skill, and retain document/revision guards. Verify semantic state and final rendered output. No model API key is required by v_ase itself.
